neutral_facts: On an evening at about 9.45 pm, the victim was sitting in the courtyard of the home with the victim's wife, talking. Four men from the same village came to the courtyard. The prosecution alleged that they said they would teach the victim a lesson for refusing to give them jaggery (gur), and that one of them fired a firearm at the victim. The shot struck the victim's right chest and arm. The victim's son and grandson, who were nearby, heard the shot, reached the courtyard within moments and reported seeing the four men fleeing. The victim was taken to a government hospital, where a doctor declared the victim dead. A written report was lodged the following day and a case was registered. The investigating officer inspected the scene, prepared an inquest report and a site plan, and seized a torch, a lantern, bloodstained soil, a bloodstained cot and bedding. Acting on information given by one accused, police recovered a 12-bore country-made pistol and one empty cartridge from a field near a transformer. The post-mortem found two firearm wounds of entry, on the right arm and right chest, with blackening and tattooing around them; death was due to shock and haemorrhage from firearm injuries, and both wounds could have been caused by one bullet. Eyewitnesses testified that the accused were armed and that one of them fired on the exhortation of the others. One eyewitness explained the source of light at the scene. The investigating officer's account differed on whether the shooting was instigated by others. Several discrepancies in the prosecution evidence were noted.
offence_severity: Maximum: death or life imprisonment (as stated in Navas quoted by the Court); minimum not stated
physical_harm: Death of 70-year-old victim from two firearm wounds of entry (right upper arm and right chest) with fractured ribs; shock and haemorrhage
number_of_offences: 2 charged (IPC s.302 r/w s.34; Arms Act s.25/27); 1 finally upheld (IPC s.302)
premeditation_planning: No premeditation found; the court held the act arose from sudden provocation
motive: Sudden provocation arising from the victim's refusal to give jaggery (gur)
key_evidence_accepted: Eyewitness testimony of P.W.1 and P.W.2; source of light explained by P.W.2; scene material objects (torch and lantern recorded in Exts.A2 and A11); recovery of country-made pistol and empty cartridge on identification by the appellant (P.W.4); post-mortem (P.W.7); prompt FIR mentioning the shooting
witness_credibility: Eyewitnesses P.W.1 and P.W.2 found reliable; discrepancies held minor and not affecting the core case; court relied on C. Muniappan on minor discrepancies
post_offence_conduct: Fled the scene after the shot (as seen by eyewitnesses); weapon later recovered on pointing out by the appellant
custody_duration: 13 years 6 months and 20 days without remission (per jail certificate); court notes more than 14 years' incarceration
bail_history: Released on bail by Supreme Court order dated 27.01.2020 on usual conditions
trial_duration: offence: 30.10.1997; trial judgment: 16.05.2006; High Court: 16.12.2011; Supreme Court: 14.10.2024
legal_representation: Appellant: Mrs. Sudha Gupta, R.S. Rathi, Ms. Kusum (Amicus Curiae/appointed counsel). State: Akshat Kumar, Ms. Anubha Dhulia
investigation_status: Written report lodged and FIR/Chik report registered (Crime No.185 of 1997); investigation completed; charge sheet filed 27.12.1997; Arms Act charge sheet filed after sanction; charges framed; trial completed
procedural_irregularity: Arms Act sanction order lacked a date (led to Arms Act acquittal); investigating Sub Inspector not examined; contradiction between the investigating officer and eyewitnesses on instigation
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted s.302 r/w s.34 IPC, life imprisonment; High Court: appeal dismissed, conviction and sentence affirmed; Supreme Court: s.302 conviction confirmed, s.34 conviction set aside, life sentence modified to period already undergone (appeal partly allowed)
prosecution_argument: Eyewitnesses P.W.1 and P.W.2 proved the appellant fired on the victim on the exhortation of co-accused; sufficient light for identification; recovery of pistol on pointing out; non-examination of witnesses not fatal; charge proved
defence_argument: No specific role in FIR; benefit of doubt should have been extended as co-accused were acquitted; source of light not in FIR; contradictions in eyewitness evidence; motive vague; eyewitness (wife) and investigating officer not examined; leniency on sentence after over 14 years
legal_principle_applied: Minor discrepancies not affecting the basic prosecution case are disregarded; benefit of doubt to co-accused not automatically extended to the appellant; s.34 requires common intention of two or more persons; sentence modification on proportionality factors (V. Sriharan, Navas)
precedent_relied_upon: Shiva Kumar @ Shiva @ Shivamurthy v. State of Karnataka [2023] 4 SCR 669 : (2023) 9 SCC 817 (followed); C. Muniappan v. State of Tamil Nadu [2010] 10 SCR 262 : (2010) 9 SCC 567 (relied on); Navas @ Mulanavas v. State of Kerala [2024] 3 SCR 913 : 2024 SCC OnLine SC 315 (relied on); Union of India v. V. Sriharan [2015] 14 SCR 613 : (2016) 7 SCC 1 (referred to); Swamy Shraddananda v. State of Karnataka [2008] 11 SCR 93 : (2008) 13 SCC 767 (referred to)
sentencing_rationale: Sudden provocation, no premeditation, no bad antecedent, poor background and family dependence, possibility of reformation, good jail conduct and over 14 years served; object of punishment includes reform and retribution, so life sentence modified to period already undergone
judicial_mitigating_factors: Sudden provocation over refusal to give jaggery; no premeditation; no bad antecedent; poor economic background and family care; good conduct in jail; possibility of reformation; acquittal under Arms Act
judicial_aggravating_factors: Gravity and nature of the offence (firearm killing) referred to generally; no specific aggravating factor expressly listed
other_sentence_order: Fine to be paid if not already paid; appellant to be set at liberty if not required in any other case; bail bond discharged
